result.name: auth_rls_initplan
result.title: Auth RLS Initialization Plan
result.description: Detects if calls to `current_setting()` and `auth.<function>()` in RLS policies are being unnecessarily re-evaluated for each row
result.detail: Table `public.projects` has a row level security policy `fixture_project_access` that re-evaluates current_setting() or auth.<function>() for each row. This produces suboptimal query performance at scale. Resolve the issue by replacing `auth.<function>()` with `(select auth.<function>())`. See [docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security#call-functions-with-select) for more info.

native.phoneCaseMapping: Changed-source refusal, local-save failure/retry and Tomorrow/Remove Date pass in the initial run. The priority case passes in the corrected rerun. The initial suite’s test assertion failure is retained; it is not reported as a green run.
native.scope: Installed reserved synthetic host, normal Store projection and real Simulator private cache and OS app relaunch. HTTP is intercepted; no task mutation is delivered to a hosted service and no real Auth/Keychain acceptance is claimed.
checks: Priority review cancellation leaves the complete cache and outbox unchanged
Save queues exactly one edit group for the two selected task identities, with notes and unselected work unchanged
Undo restores every original task row and queues a fresh linked edit group; normal app relaunch preserves the exact saved cache
Tomorrow writes the expected calendar day to both selected tasks and leaves the unselected third row intact
Explicit Remove Date supports saved rows with omitted optional clock fields
Changed saved contents disable the complete review and produce no queued change
Injected local persistence failure keeps tasks/outbox unchanged; the same review retries to exactly one group

diagnostics: Before the production fix, the sparse-row Core regression failed in TeamTaskEditScope.body because absent optional clock keys did not satisfy validation. Validation now normalizes a temporary copy, while the persisted/wire source record remains unchanged. Opening identity/access and whole-row checks remain intact.

The initial phone priority test incorrectly searched the entire app, including the underlying list behind the review sheet, for the unselected task. The assertion now searches the review form. Three other scenario methods were unchanged; the corrected priority scenario passes and the final iPad suite passes all four.
